objective_changes.statement: Where Processing Integrity is in scope, the published terms or service description say what the service processes, which inputs it accepts and what customers can expect about the completeness, accuracy and timing of its outputs.
objective_changes.why: SOC2:PI1.1 is mapped partial to CS-02 on the published terms, and no objective tested what those terms say about processing.

objective_changes.statement: A security reporting channel, such as a security address or form, is published for staff and customers. It names who reads it and the expected response time, says that reports made in good faith carry no blame, and the incident plan points to it.
objective_changes.why: The ISO27001:A.6.8 mapping is full and its rationale relies on no blame for good faith reports, which no objective tested.

objective_changes.statement: The company belonged to or subscribed to security groups and advisory feeds that fit its technology and sector, and a named person followed each one and passed on what mattered.
objective_changes.why: Moves with ISO27001:A.5.6 to the successor control.

objective_changes.statement: The security groups, advisory feeds and professional bodies the company follows are listed, each chosen for its technology or sector, with a named owner and a rule for what is passed on and to whom.
objective_changes.why: The successor needs a design objective of its own.

objective_changes.statement: Items passed on from these sources in the period reached the threat review or the people named, and the list of sources was checked in the last 12 months.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.5.6 is about keeping the contact useful, so what came of it is tested, not membership alone.

objective_changes.statement: Software licences and other intellectual property terms the company relies on are in the register with their limits and an owner, and use was compared with those limits in the last 12 months.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.5.32 is mapped partial on licence and IP terms in the register, and no objective tested them.

objective_changes.statement: Every deficiency found in the period was logged with its source, date found, owner, severity, root cause, due date and the step taken at once to contain it and deal with its effects, including those raised by internal audit and by incidents.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:10.2 is mapped full and its rationale names containment and consequences, which the objective left out.

objective_changes.statement: Deficiencies past their due date were reported at management review with a new date or a decision.
objective_changes.why: The old objective bundled overdue reporting with the search for the same cause elsewhere; the second part moves to GOV-08.F.

objective_changes.statement: Where a root cause could apply elsewhere, other systems and teams were checked for the same problem, and the policy, procedure or control was changed where the cause showed a wider gap.
objective_changes.why: Tests the part of ISO27001:10.2 on similar problems elsewhere and changes to the program on its own.

objective_changes.statement: After each significant change to the organization, its services or the way security is run, a targeted independent review was held, or the change was recorded as covered by the next planned audit with a reason.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.5.35 is mapped full and expects review on significant change as well as at planned intervals.

objective_changes.statement: Where the Privacy category is in scope, the audit program covers the privacy commitments, including how privacy requests and complaints are handled.
objective_changes.why: SOC2:P8.1 is mapped partial to GOV-13 (guided onboarding part 5, section 7) with no objective behind it.

objective_changes.statement: An approved procedure sets a management review at least each quarter with the security lead and managers who can commit resources, and states how actions are recorded and escalated.
objective_changes.why: The input list of the yearly review moves to GOV-31.A.

objective_changes.statement: In the last 12 months top management judged whether the program still fits the business, covers what it should and works, using the set inputs, and recorded its decisions on improvements, changes and resources.
objective_changes.why: Moves with ISO27001:9.3.1 to 9.3.3 to the successor control.

objective_changes.statement: An approved procedure sets a review by top management at least once a year and lists what it must take in: actions from earlier reviews, changes in outside and inside factors and in what interested parties need, their feedback, nonconformities and corrective actions, measurement and audit results, how far objectives were met, risk results and treatment status, and improvement ideas.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:9.3.2 needs the inputs set in advance.

objective_changes.statement: The record of the yearly review shows each listed input was considered, with the source record for each, or says why one did not apply.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:9.3.2 is tested input by input, which the old GOV-15.C did in one line.

objective_changes.statement: Each decision from the yearly review on improvements, changes to the program or resources has an owner and a date and was tracked to closure or carried to the next review.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:9.3.3 outputs are tested on their own.

objective_changes.statement: The top level security policy is approved by top management, or by the board where a regulator requires it. It fits the purpose of the company, states the security objectives or how they are set, and commits to meeting the requirements that apply and to improving the program.
objective_changes.why: Moves with ISO27001:5.2 to the successor control.

objective_changes.statement: The current version of each policy was available to all staff at a known location during the period.
objective_changes.why: The part on sharing the top level policy outside the company moves to GOV-32.D.

objective_changes.statement: The current policy statement was communicated to staff and made available to customers and other interested parties who need it, and the version they could reach was the approved one.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:5.2 expects the statement communicated inside and available outside; this was half of the old GOV-17.D.

objective_changes.statement: Each risk treated by transfer names the contract or insurance policy that carries it, with its cover and expiry, and a recorded decision says whether insurance is needed against business disruption.
objective_changes.why: SOC2:CC9.1 is mapped partial to GOV-20 and the guided onboarding plan adds the insurance decision; no objective tested transfer.

objective_changes.statement: Each person holding a role with security duties was told of the role and its duties in writing, such as through a role description they acknowledged, and could describe it when asked.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:5.3 expects roles to be communicated, and the mapping rationale says this control does not show it; no other control did.

objective_changes.statement: A list names every document and record the program needs, including those the standards, laws and contracts followed call for, each with an owner.
objective_changes.why: The operating procedures part moves to GOV-28.F, so ISO27001:7.5.1 and A.5.37 are tested apart.

objective_changes.statement: An operating procedure exists for each routine task on the systems in scope, with an owner, version and review date, and the people who run those systems can reach the current version.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.5.37 is owned by engineering and was folded into the documents list objective.

objective_changes.statement: Before each planned change to the management system or the services in scope, the reason, expected effect, owner, timing and resources were recorded and approved.
objective_changes.why: Planned and unplanned changes are two populations; unplanned ones move to GOV-29.F.

objective_changes.statement: Each unplanned change to the management system or the services in scope in the period was reviewed afterwards for harm, and any action needed was raised.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:8.1 asks for unintended changes to be reviewed, tested on its own.

objective_changes.statement: The list of staff and contractors who started in the period was complete when compared with the joiner roster and the contractor register.
objective_changes.why: Outside parties are a different population with a different source; they move to HR-02.F.

objective_changes.statement: Each outside party given confidential information in the period, such as a supplier, partner or prospective customer, had a non-disclosure agreement or contract confidentiality terms in force first.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.6.6 is mapped full and covers outside parties, whose population is the vendor and partner list, not the joiner roster.

objective_changes.statement: Every leaver on the roster for the period had a closed offboarding record.
objective_changes.why: Role changes move to HR-05.F.

objective_changes.statement: Each role change in the period had the access, asset and duty items of the checklist run by the date of the change, and access the new role does not need was removed.
objective_changes.why: ISO27001:A.6.5 covers change of role; movers and leavers are separate populations with separate failures.

objective_changes.statement: The training checked that people understood it, such as through a quiz or a phishing exercise, and each person below the pass mark was trained again.
objective_changes.why: The SOC2:CC1.4 rationale says attendance alone does not show competence, and ISO27001:A.6.3 and 7.2 expect training to work.
